The orthorhombic Ca4Ge4O12 structure (reduced formula CaGeO3, space group Amm2, No. 38) has 20 atoms per unit cell distributed over seven independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Ca centers coordinated by eight O neighbors and Ge centers coordinated by four O neighbors. O environments involve Ca and Ge neighbors, with one O orbit having eight geometric neighbors (two Ca and six Ge). Validated polyhedron contacts include corner- and face-sharing between Ca- and Ge-centered polyhedra and corner-sharing among Ge-centered polyhedra, forming a three-dimensional connectivity network.
